raw_case_text: A 50-year-old male livestock farmer was admitted to Sparta General Hospital with a 4-day history of fever, malaise, night sweats, and shortness of breath. He had been diagnosed with blood culture proven Brucella infection 6 months ago and was treated with a double regimen of 21 days of streptomycin and two months of doxycycline. He had recovered completely and Brucella antibodies titers were negative after two months of treatment. On admission, he was febrile (38.7 C) and physical examination revealed cervical lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, and a 2/6 diastolic aortic murmur not reported in his previous medical history. According to CBC he was anemic (Ht 24%) and leukopenic (3.200/muL), ESR was 102 mm/h, and biochemistry revealed a serum creatinine value of 2.1 mg/dL while BUN levels were 92 mg/dL. Wright standard tube agglutination test was positive in a titer of 1 : 1600. Blood cultures were positive for Brucella spp. that was identified later as melitensis. In transthoracic echocardiogram, vegetations were present on a bicuspid aortic valve (Figure 1). A triple antibiotic regimen with 900 mg of rifampicin, 200 mg of doxycycline daily, and streptomycin adjusted for renal failure was initiated. Transesophageal echocardiogram was performed the next day and confirmed the presence of active vegetations but also revealed severe aortic regurgitation and rupture of the noncoronary leaflet. He was referred for cardiothoracic consultation and a valve replacement surgery was decided. During hospitalization, fever, malaise, and renal failure had gradually resolved, but he developed decompensated heart failure requiring loop diuretics and oxygen supplementation. On the 21st day of treatment, streptomycin has been replaced with cotrimoxazole and three days later valve replacement was performed. The patient recovered without any surgical complications, continued antibiotic treatment for 6 months, and is currently well.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 50-year-old male livestock farmer with a bicuspid aortic valve presented with a 4-day history of fever (38.7 °C), malaise, night sweats, and shortness of breath.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Six months prior to admission, the patient had been treated for a blood culture-proven systemic bacterial infection with streptomycin (21 days) and doxycycline (2 months), achieving complete recovery and negative antibody titers. Four days prior to this admission, he developed acute fever, malaise, night sweats, and shortness of breath. During hospitalization, he developed decompensated heart failure requiring loop diuretics and oxygen supplementation.
subjective.past_medical_history: Underlying congenital bicuspid aortic valve. History of blood culture-proven systemic bacterial infection 6 months prior, treated with 21 days of streptomycin and 2 months of doxycycline. Occupation: livestock farmer in Sparta, Greece. Prior drug allergies not documented.
subjective.review_of_systems: Shortness of breath, night sweats, fever, malaise. Home medications: completed prior course of streptomycin and doxycycline; received loop diuretics during hospitalization. Allergies: not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Temperature: 38.7 °C. Lymphatics: cervical lymphadenopathy. Abdomen: hepatosplenomegaly. Cardiovascular: grade 2/6 diastolic aortic murmur (new finding). Developed clinical signs of decompensated heart failure during admission.
objective.routine_investigations: CBC: hematocrit 24% (anemic), WBC 3,200/muL (leukopenic). Inflammatory markers: ESR 102 mm/h. Renal function: serum creatinine 2.1 mg/dL, BUN 92 mg/dL (acute renal failure, which gradually resolved). Transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE): vegetations present on a bicuspid aortic valve.
objective.advanced_workup: Transesophageal echocardiogram (TEE): confirmed active vegetations, severe aortic regurgitation, and rupture of the noncoronary aortic valve leaflet. Emergency cardiothoracic surgery: aortic valve replacement surgery on day 24 of hospitalization.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Relapsed brucellar native bicuspid aortic valve endocarditis complicated by leaflet rupture, severe aortic regurgitation, decompensated heart failure, and acute renal failure.
Confirmation: Wright standard tube agglutination test positive at a titer of 1:1600; blood cultures positive for Brucella spp., subsequently identified as Brucella melitensis.
Differentials ruled out: Non-brucellar infective endocarditis and non-infectious acute aortic insufficiency ruled out by blood culture isolation of B. melitensis and echocardiography.
Treatment & Outcome: Triple antibiotic regimen initiated with oral rifampicin (900 mg daily), oral doxycycline (200 mg daily), and renal-adjusted streptomycin. On day 21, streptomycin was switched to cotrimoxazole. On day 24, successful surgical aortic valve replacement was performed. The patient recovered without surgical complications, completed a 6-month course of antibiotic therapy, and remained healthy on follow-up.
